info.title: Pylota Identity API
info.summary: Email and identity for AI agents, running on your own Cloudflare account.
info.description:
The machine-readable contract for the Pylota Identity REST API. `docs/src/reference/api.md` is the
readable version; if the two disagree, this document is the contract. A running deployment serves
the same document, generated from the Rust types (`crates/api-types`, utoipa), at `/openapi.json`.

## Conventions

- **Base URL.** Versioned endpoints live under `https://{host}/v1`. `/health`, `/openapi.json`,
  `/hooks/ses`, `/hooks/ses/inbound` and the `/.well-known/*` documents live at the host root; their
  path items override `servers`.
- **Authentication.** `Authorization: Bearer pmk_live_…` (or `pmk_test_…`). Only `/health`,
  `/openapi.json`, `/v1/plans`, `/.well-known/*`, `/v1/links/{token}`, `POST /v1/agent-signup`,
  `/hooks/ses` and `/hooks/ses/inbound` are unauthenticated. `/v1/links/{token}` is checked by its
  signature (`GET` for downloads, `PUT` for upload bytes), and the two `/hooks/ses*` endpoints by the
  SNS signature (version 2 only). `GET /v1/events/stream` also accepts a single-use stream token in
  `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` (`streamToken`), never in the URL.
- **Not described here.** The server-rendered console (`/console/*`, including `/console/sign-in…`,
  `/console/sign-up`, `/console/waitlist`, `/console/workspaces/new`,
  `/console/oauth/{provider}/start`, `/console/oauth/{provider}/callback`,
  `/console/settings/security`, `/console/settings/notifications`, `/console/plan/return`,
  `/console/connect`, the agent sign-up pages `/console/agent-signup/verify`, `/console/agent-signup/claim`
  and `/console/agent-signup/refuse`, and the notification unsubscribe pair
  `/console/notifications/unsubscribe`) and
  `/billing/stripe/webhook` (Stripe events) are served by the same Worker but are not part of the
  developer API: they use session cookies, OAuth state, unsubscribe tokens and Stripe signatures, not
  API keys.
- **Hosts.** The console answers on `PM_CONSOLE_HOST`, which defaults to `PM_API_HOST`. When the two
  differ, console paths answer only on `PM_CONSOLE_HOST`, and the API host `PM_API_HOST` serves only
  the REST API (`/v1/*`), MCP (`/mcp`), `/openapi.json`, `/health`, `/.well-known/*`, signed links
  (`/v1/links/*`), `/hooks/*` and `/billing/stripe/webhook`; anything else returns
  `404 route_not_found`, and no cookie is set or read on the API host. A route called with a method
  it does not have returns `405 method_not_allowed` with an `Allow` header.
- **Format.** JSON (`application/json; charset=utf-8`). Times are RFC 3339 UTC strings. Sizes are bytes.
- **IDs** are a type prefix, an underscore and a 26-character upper-case Crockford base32 ULID
  (`ten_ idn_ adr_ dom_ thr_ msg_ att_ whk_ dlv_ evt_ key_ era_ exp_ job_ aud_ req_ usr_ inv_ dlq_ hld_ prb_ ptn_ sac_ drf_ evc_ wsc_ sfb_ upl_ asu_`).
- **Pagination.** List endpoints take `limit` (default 25, max 100) and `cursor`, and return
  `{ "data": [...], "next_cursor": "…" | null }`. Cursors are opaque and expire after 24 hours
  (`410 cursor_expired`). A list cursor is keyset-based (`created_at`, then `id`, newest first),
  MACed under the deployment's cursor key and bound to the operation, its filters and the calling key;
  one used elsewhere, altered, or signed by an unknown key is `400 invalid_request` (path `cursor`).
  Two exceptions: the event log (`/events` and `/event-consumers/{consumer_id}/events`) pages by log
  position, with its own `limit` (1–500, default 100) and cursors that expire only when retention
  removes the events behind them; the tenant's queue of drafts (`/tenants/{tenant_id}/drafts`) lists
  oldest first.
- **Idempotency.** `Idempotency-Key` is required on send, reply, reply-all, forward, calendar-reply
  and draft send (`…/drafts/{draft_id}/send`), except on a dry run (`dry_run=true`), where it is
  optional and never recorded. It is optional on every other `POST` except ten
  (`x-idempotency: none`), which ignore it and never record it: the two search endpoints
  (`/identities/{identity_id}/search` and `/tenants/{tenant_id}/search`, which return mail and change
  nothing, so no record ever stores their results), `batch-get`
  (`/identities/{identity_id}/messages/batch-get`, for the same reason), the two signing endpoints
  (`…/assertions` and `…/http-signatures`), the two SNS endpoints (`/hooks/ses` and
  `/hooks/ses/inbound`), `/events/stream-tokens`, because each call mints a single-use secret that a
  stored replay would have to keep or drop, `/agent-signup` (no key), whose answer holds a key secret
  for the same reason, and the mailbox restore (`/platform/identities/{identity_id}/restore`). No
  stored replay ever holds mail content: a replayed response that carries a
  message, thread or draft (release, cancel, resolve, hold, the draft routes) re-reads the resource
  with the caller's visibility. Keys are kept for 30 days, scoped per
  identity for mail, and per calling API key and tenant (or partner, or deployment, when the request
  names no tenant) for everything else. A replay returns the original response with the header
  `Idempotent-Replayed: true` (and `"deduplicated": true` in mail responses); a response that carried
  a one-time secret is replayed without it and with `"secret_replayed": false`.
- **Rate limits.** Every authenticated response carries `RateLimit-Limit`: the limit of the bucket that
  applied, per period. A `429` also carries `Retry-After` and `RateLimit-Reset`, the seconds to the end
  of the bucket's current period; for `rate_limited` the two are equal, and the other `429` codes set
  `Retry-After` to their own wait. `RateLimit-Remaining` is not sent: the Workers rate-limiting binding
  answers only allow or deny, so the Worker cannot know how many requests are left.
- **Errors.** Every non-2xx response uses the `Error` envelope, whose `docs` links to the code's entry on
  the deployment's published errors page (`PM_DOCS_URL`). Handle unknown error codes by HTTP status.
- **Evolution.** Additive changes (new fields, new event types, new enum values) can happen within
  `/v1`. Clients must ignore unknown fields and handle unknown enum values, even where this document
  lists an `enum`.
- **Untrusted content.** Every text field that comes from email (subjects, display names, filenames,
  bodies, attachment text, snippets) is untrusted. Show it to a model inside a clearly delimited block,
  never as instructions.

## Vendor extensions

| Extension | On | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `x-required-permission` | operation | Array of permissions the key must hold, all of them. `[]` means any valid key |
| `x-required-permission-any` | operation | Array of permissions of which the key must hold at least one. Used with `x-required-permission: []` |
| `x-key-levels` | operation | Key levels (`platform`, `partner`, `tenant`, `identity`) that can call the operation at all. A `partner` key acts only on the tenants its partner's keys created |
| `x-permission-notes` | operation | Conditional permission or scope rules that the two fields above cannot express |
| `x-rate-limit-buckets` | operation | Rate-limit buckets the request counts against (`api`, `search`, `agentic`, `send`, `sign`, `partner`, `signin`; `partner` only for a partner key's calls; `signin` per client network, shared with the console's sign-in forms) |
| `x-idempotency` | operation | `required`, `optional` or `none` for the `Idempotency-Key` header. `required` means a request without it fails with `400 idempotency_key_required`, except a dry run (`dry_run=true`). `none` means the header is ignored and never recorded |
| `x-error-codes` | response | The `error.code` values this operation can return with that status |
| `x-sdk` | operation | `false` when neither SDK (Rust or TypeScript) has a method for the operation: the SES hooks, which only Amazon SNS calls, and `security.txt`. Every other operation has exactly one method in each SDK |

tags.name: Meta
tags.description: Health, the OpenAPI document and the calling key.

tags.name: Tenants
tags.description: Tenants and their policy. Keys with `tenants:manage`: platform keys for every tenant, partner keys for the tenants their partner's keys created. The tenant's own policy route also takes tenant keys with `policy:write`.

tags.name: Partners
tags.description: Partners: integrators whose partner keys create tenants and act only on those tenants. Platform keys with `partners:manage`.

tags.name: Identities
tags.description: Agent identities (one mailbox each).

tags.name: Addresses
tags.description: The addresses of an identity, with promotion to primary and retirement.

tags.name: Identity keys
tags.description: An identity's Ed25519 signing keys, agent assertions (signed JWTs) and signed HTTP requests (Web Bot Auth). Private keys never leave the Worker and no endpoint returns them.

tags.name: Service accounts
tags.description: The service sign-up ledger: third-party accounts an agent asks to create with its identity's address, and the operator's approvals (FR-IDN-10). `accounts:request` and `accounts:approve`.

tags.name: Phone numbers
tags.description: Catalogue, onboarding, the standing budget, one-call purchase, numbers, requests, compliance, registrations, voice connectors, port-outs and charges.

tags.name: SMS and calls
tags.description: Sending and receiving SMS, waiting for codes, calls, consent.

tags.name: Vault
tags.description: Logins, API keys and browser sessions that agents use without seeing them: items, grants, uses, tickets, consumers, custody and the vault audit (FR-VLT). Values are write-only. The consumer routes take no API key: they are authenticated by an RFC 9421 signature (`vaultConsumerSignature`).

tags.name: Agent sign-up
tags.description: Self-sign-up for agents on Pylota Identity Cloud (FR-ASU), behind `PM_AGENT_SIGNUP`. One unauthenticated call creates a provisional workspace, one inbox and one key; the named human verifies with a code or a link; unverified workspaces are erased after 7 days.

tags.name: Domains
tags.description: The platform domain and tenant domains, DNS records and health.

tags.name: Threads
tags.description: Threads in an identity's mailbox.

tags.name: Messages
tags.description: Messages, raw MIME, attachments, triage and quarantine release.

tags.name: Sending
tags.description: Send, reply, reply-all, forward, calendar-reply, cancel and resolve. `Idempotency-Key` is required on the first five, except on a dry run (`dry_run=true`).

tags.name: Drafts
tags.description: Drafts, approval before send and scheduled send (FR-DRF). `drafts:read`, `drafts:write`, `drafts:approve`; sending a draft needs `messages:send`.

tags.name: Uploads
tags.description: Files staged by an identity and attached to its sends by `upload_id`. Create, `PUT` the bytes to the signed `upload_url`, attach. `messages:send` or `drafts:write`.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Keyword, semantic, hybrid and agentic search, related messages, contacts and `wait`.

tags.name: Quarantine
tags.description: Quarantined mail.

tags.name: Screening
tags.description: Screening of inbound mail for agent steering (FR-SCR): feedback on a verdict and the per-identity and per-tenant summaries.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Webhook endpoints, deliveries and replay. Reads need `webhooks:read`; everything else needs `webhooks:manage`, which includes `webhooks:read`.

tags.name: Event feed
tags.description: The tenant's event log: the feed, durable event consumers, stream tokens and the WebSocket stream. Every operation needs `events:read`.

tags.name: Suppressions
tags.description: Suppressed recipients.

tags.name: Lists
tags.description: Receive and send allow and block lists.

tags.name: Keys
tags.description: API keys.

tags.name: Privacy
tags.description: Erasure requests and subject-access exports.

tags.name: Usage
tags.description: Plan, allowances, usage figures, the plan catalog and workspace billing accounts.

tags.name: Audit
tags.description: Audit log.

tags.name: Metrics
tags.description: Pause-window rates with thresholds and headroom, and event counts per hour or day. `metrics:read`.

tags.name: Members
tags.description: Console members and invitations of a workspace. `members:manage`, tenant, partner and platform keys.

tags.name: Platform
tags.description: Platform operations: signing-key rotation, the dead-letter queue, maintenance jobs, waitlist invitations and the list of agent sign-ups. Platform keys with `platform:ops`; every call is audit-logged.

tags.name: Links and hooks
tags.description: Signed links (downloads and upload bytes) and the two Amazon SES notification endpoints (delivery events and inbound mail). No API key.

tags.name: Well-known
tags.description: Documents served at `/.well-known/` on the API host: the security contact, each identity's JWK Set and the Web Bot Auth key directory. No API key.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Webhook events delivered to your endpoints (Standard Webhooks).

post.description: An inbound message is stored and visible.

data.extracted_text: Could we move the pick-up to Friday at 10?

post.description: An inbound message is stored but quarantined.
A quarantined message was released.
Triage finished (or failed).

A screening verdict was reached for an inbound message (or decided at ingest), or a late signal changed it. It always precedes, by one `sequence`, the `message.received` or `message.quarantined` it causes. No subject, address or text; an endpoint subscribed to it needs `quarantine:review`.
The transport accepted an outbound message.
A recipient's server accepted the message.
A temporary failure; the provider is retrying.
A permanent failure, or retries exhausted.
A recipient reported spam.
The transport refused the message before sending.
The message could not be sent.
The outcome is unknown; the message is never resent automatically.
An uncertain send was matched to a provider event.
Every recipient is suppressed; nothing was sent.
The message was cancelled while queued.
Opt-in: labels of visible messages changed. Sent only when the tenant policy has `events.labels_changed: true` and only to endpoints that name the type.
A verification code or link was found in authenticated mail. The value itself is only available through `wait`.
A message with a calendar object became visible as received: when stored, released, or re-parsed with a changed object. Never for quarantined, screening, hidden or throttled mail.
A draft waits for approval, or was edited while waiting, or a send found approval needed. Thin: no subject, body, address, filename or note.
An approver approved a revision of a draft.
An approver rejected a draft, or its approval request expired after 7 days.
A draft became a message; the message emits its own `message.*` events.
A scheduled or approved send of a draft ended without a message. A failed draft is never retried automatically.
An identity was created.
An identity was updated.
An identity was paused (manually, for abuse, or because its tenant was suspended).
A paused identity was resumed.

An identity was deleted: emitted once, when the identity-scope erasure that deletes it completes and the identity becomes `deleted` (after held threads are released, if any). It comes from the erasure job with `identity_id` set.
An address was added to an identity.
A pending address became active once its domain was healthy.
An address became the identity's primary.
An address became retired.

A signing key was created for an identity that had no active key, lazily by a signing request or by `POST …/keys`. Not sent when `POST …/keys` returns the existing active key; the new key of a rotation emits `identity.key_rotated` instead.
An identity signing key was rotated: `kid` is the new active key and `previous_kid` the key now `retiring` (`null` when the rotation created the first key).
An identity signing key was revoked and is `retired`; it has left the identity's JWK Set. Not sent for a key that was already `retired`.
A domain was added.
A domain became healthy for the first time.
A domain became degraded.
A domain started failing; sending falls back to platform addresses unless disabled by policy.
A domain was suspended; ownership must be re-proved.
A domain returned to healthy.
A domain is still unhealthy (sent at 24 h, 72 h and 7 days in the state).

A domain was removed: on request (`reason: requested`), because Cloudflare deleted a `nameservers` zone that was never activated (`reason: zone_expired`), because another tenant proved control of the DNS of a domain this tenant never verified (`reason: evicted`), or because it was never verified within 14 days (`reason: unverified_expired`).
An erasure request completed, with its receipt.
An erasure step failed after the job runner's own retries.
A subject-access export is ready. Fetch the download link from the API.
An address was suppressed.
A quota reached 80% or 100% of its limit.

A webhook endpoint was disabled. Sent to platform endpoints and, when the disabled endpoint belongs to a partner (a partner endpoint, or an endpoint of a tenant a partner's key created), to that partner's other endpoints; never to tenant endpoints or to the endpoint itself.
A test event sent by `POST /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}/test`.
An invitation to the workspace was created or re-sent.
An invitation was accepted; the user is now a member.
A member's role changed (an ownership transfer sends two).
A member was removed, or left.
The workspace's plan changed.
A payment failed; the workspace keeps its plan until `grace_until`.
A plan allowance is spent. Sent once per feature per period, when the first `402 billing_limit` is returned.
A tenant's policy was changed (any route, any writer, except a tenant's creation).
A provisional agent sign-up was verified by its human.
An agent recorded that it wants an account at a third-party service.
An operator approved a service-ledger entry.
A service-ledger entry was rejected by an operator, or expired after 7 days undecided.
A service-ledger entry was closed, or deleted while pending or approved.
An inbound SMS is stored and visible.
An inbound SMS is stored but held. `sms.text` is absent.
A held SMS was released.
A screening verdict on an SMS.
A verification code was found in a visible SMS. The value is only available through `GET …/sms/wait`.
The provider accepted the SMS.
The handset or carrier confirmed delivery.
The SMS was refused or not delivered.
The carrier gave no final answer.
The outcome is unknown; it is never resent automatically.
An uncertain SMS was matched to a provider record.
A call on one of the identity's numbers began.
A call ended, or a call record filled it in later.
A phone request was created, or returned to `pending_approval` because its price rose.
A person, an allowed key or the tenant's standing budget approved a phone request.
A phone request was rejected, or expired after 7 days.
A phone request was canceled by the requester, or by erasure.
The provider work of a phone request ended successfully.
The provider work of a phone request ended without success.
A billable provider call's outcome is unknown; the service is reconciling.
A number changed status.
One of a number's capability facets changed state.
A number bought with `expires_at` will be released within 24 hours.
The provider needs information before a deadline.
Another carrier asked for the number.
A person authorised or rejected a port-out, or the provider authorised it.
A US 10DLC brand, campaign or number assignment, or a toll-free verification, changed status.
The compliance profile's status for a country, number type and action changed.
A counterparty opted out or in.
Phone spend reached 80% or 100% of a monthly cap.
The tenant's onboarding status for a country changed.
The tenant's standing purchase budget was set, loosened, tightened or turned off.
A vault item was created or imported.
A vault item's metadata, origins, approval level or state changed.
A new version of a vault item became current.
A vault item was crypto-shredded.
A person revealed a value in the console, or was shown a new managed value once.
A vault item's health changed.
An agent asked for a vault grant.
A vault grant was approved, or created approved.
A vault grant was denied.
A vault grant was revoked, or given up by its agent.
A vault grant's pending week or active period ended.
The orchestrator created a vault use (also for refusals at creation).
A person must decide on a vault use.
A vault use was approved; mint a ticket now.
A vault use was denied.
A vault use's approval deadline or first-redemption window passed.
The orchestrator canceled a vault use.
A vault use closed, normally or early.
A vault ticket was minted.
A consumer redeemed a phase.
A redemption was refused.
A consumer reported an outcome.
A vault consumer was registered, activated, suspended, resumed, re-keyed or revoked.
The tenant's vault key rotated, custody changed, or `revoke-all` ran.

apiKey.description: An API key sent as a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer pmk_live_…`. Keys have a level (`platform`, `tenant` or `identity`) and a list of permissions; scope always comes from the key, never from the request body (FR-KEY-3). Only a keyed hash of the secret is stored.

streamToken.name: Sec-WebSocket-Protocol
streamToken.description: Only for `GET /events/stream`: the subprotocol list `pylota-identity.events.v1, pylota-identity.token.{token}` with a token from `createStreamToken`. Single use, 60 seconds. Never echoed.

vaultConsumerSignature.name: Signature
vaultConsumerSignature.description: Only for `/v1/vault/consumer/*`: an RFC 9421 HTTP message signature made with the consumer's Ed25519 key, labelled `sig1`, over `("@method" "@authority" "@path" "content-digest")` (three components for `GET`), with `created`, `expires` (at most 60 seconds after `created`), a `nonce` of 16–64 random bytes, `keyid` (the RFC 7638 thumbprint of the consumer's signing JWK), `alg="ed25519"` and `tag="pylota-identity-vault-consumer"`. API keys are refused on these routes.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Opaque; expires after 24 hours (`410 cursor_expired`).

After.name: after
After.description: Only items at or after this time (RFC 3339).

Include.name: include
Include.description: Comma-separated extras for each message: `quoted` adds the full plain `text`, `html` adds the sanitised `html`, `headers` adds the original `headers`.

TenantIdQuery.name: tenant_id
TenantIdQuery.description: Restrict to one tenant. A platform key may name any tenant; a partner key, one of its own tenants; a tenant or identity key, only its own (a list is always restricted to it). A tenant outside the key's scope returns `404 tenant_not_found`, never an empty page, as for a missing tenant.

IdempotencyKeySend.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeySend.description: Required on every real send, reply, reply-all, forward, calendar-reply and draft send; optional on a dry run (`dry_run=true`), where it is never recorded. 1–255 printable ASCII characters, unique per message. Kept for 30 days, scoped to the identity. Reuse the same key on every retry of the same request. Missing: `400 idempotency_key_required`; malformed: `400 invalid_idempotency_key`.

DryRun.name: dry_run
DryRun.description: `true` runs every check (permissions, policy, recipients, suppressions and lists, size) without sending or storing anything, taking quota or locking the thread, and returns `200` with a `DryRunResult`. `Idempotency-Key` is optional and never recorded.

IdempotencyKeyOptional.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyOptional.description: Optional. 1–255 printable ASCII characters. Kept for 30 days, scoped to the calling API key and the tenant (or, for a request that names no tenant, to the partner for a partner key and to the platform for a platform key), so another key never receives this key's replay. The same key with the same request returns the original response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; with a different request, `409 idempotency_conflict`. A response that carried a one-time secret (`createKey`, `rotateKey`, `createWebhook`, `createTenantWebhook`, `rotateWebhookSecret`) is replayed without it and with `"secret_replayed": false`.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: The draft's `etag`; a stale value fails with `409 draft_revision_mismatch`. `*` matches any draft.

EventAfter.name: after
EventAfter.description: A cursor from a previous page, `earliest` (the oldest retained event comes next) or `latest`. Not with `since`.

EventSince.name: since
EventSince.description: Start with the first event appended at or after this time. Not with `after`; not in the future.

EventIdentityFilter.name: identity_id
EventIdentityFilter.description: Identity IDs, comma-separated, at most 100. An identity key may name only its own.

EventWait.name: wait
EventWait.description: Seconds to wait for a matching event when none is newer.

ScreeningFrom.name: from
ScreeningFrom.description: Start of the window (RFC 3339). Default 30 days before `to`.

ScreeningTo.name: to
ScreeningTo.description: End of the window (RFC 3339). Default now. At most 92 days after `from`.

IdentityKeyKidPath.name: kid
IdentityKeyKidPath.description: The identity key's ID, its RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint (base64url, 43 characters).

SigningKeyPurposePath.name: purpose
SigningKeyPurposePath.description: `thread` (thread tokens), `link` (download links, console sign-in, invitation and session tokens, OAuth state hashes), `cursor` (search cursors) or `web_bot_auth` (Web Bot Auth HTTP signatures and the key directory).

LinkTokenPath.name: token
LinkTokenPath.description: The signed-link token. It carries the signing key's kid and an expiry.

ListEntryPath.name: entry
ListEntryPath.description: An address (`user@example.com`) or a whole domain (`@example.com`), percent-encoded where needed.

WebhookIdHeader.name: webhook-id
WebhookIdHeader.description: The event ID. Delivery is at least once, so deduplicate on it.

WebhookTimestampHeader.name: webhook-timestamp
WebhookTimestampHeader.description: Unix time in seconds when the delivery was signed. Reject requests more than 5 minutes from your clock.

WebhookSignatureHeader.name: webhook-signature
WebhookSignatureHeader.description: Space-separated `v1,<base64>` signatures: `base64(HMAC-SHA256(secret_bytes, "{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}"))`, where `secret_bytes` is the base64-decoded part of `whsec_…` after the prefix. Two signatures are sent during a secret rotation overlap. Compare in constant time and accept on any match.

IdempotencyKeyRequired.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyRequired.description: Required on every phone and vault route marked `x-idempotency: required`: those that can cost money, move a number, decide a request or grant, or create a vault use. 1–255 printable ASCII characters; reuse the same key on every retry of the same request. Kept for 30 days, scoped to the calling API key and the tenant. The same key with the same request returns the original response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; with a different request, `409 idempotency_conflict`. A response that carried a vault ticket or an unlock key is replayed without it. Missing: `400 idempotency_key_required`; malformed: `400 invalid_idempotency_key`.

IdempotencyKeySms.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeySms.description: Required on every real SMS send; optional on a dry run, where it is never recorded.

VaultUnlockHeader.name: X-Pylota-Identity-Vault-Unlock
VaultUnlockHeader.description: Partner custody only: an unlock key (`pvu_` + 52 Crockford base32 characters), accepted only from the tenant's own partner key on the unwrapping routes. Never logged, stored or echoed.

VaultContentDigest.name: Content-Digest
VaultContentDigest.description: RFC 9530 `sha-256=:<base64>:` of the body as sent.

Request-Id.description: The request ID (`req_…`). Every response carries it, and errors echo it as `error.request_id`.

RateLimit-Limit.description: The limit of the rate-limit bucket that applied to this request, per period (for example `600` for the per-key bucket of 600 requests a minute). Every authenticated response carries it.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Sent only with a `429`: seconds until the end of the bucket's current period. There is no `RateLimit-Remaining` header, because the rate-limiting binding answers only allow or deny.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. On a `429 rate_limited` it equals `RateLimit-Reset`.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: Present, with the value `true`, when the response is a replay of an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

ETag.description: The draft's entity tag, `"{revision}-{8 hex}"`. Send it back in `If-Match`.

Content-Disposition-Attachment.description: Always `attachment`, with the sanitised filename, for example `attachment; filename="INV-88213.pdf"`.

Cache-Control-Jwks.description: Always `public, max-age=300`. Verifiers cache an identity's JWK Set for at most 5 minutes.

Directory-Signature-Input.description: One RFC 9421 signature per listed key, each over `("@authority";req)` with `alg="ed25519"`, `keyid` (the key's JWK thumbprint), a 64-byte random `nonce`, `tag="http-message-signatures-directory"`, `created` and `expires` (`created` + 300).

Directory-Signature.description: The signatures named in `Signature-Input`, one per listed key.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed or violates the schema. `details.errors[]` holds `{path, message}`.

SendBadRequest.description: The send request is invalid. `too_many_recipients`: more than `policy.max_recipients` (hard maximum 49: Cloudflare allows 50 and one is kept for the hidden journal copy). A `from_address` that is not allowed is `invalid_request` with `details.errors[0].path = "from_address"`. `too_many_recipients` with `details.reason = "calendar_single_recipient"`: a calendar message on the `cloudflare` transport when a raw send takes one recipient. The `calendar_*` codes refuse an iCalendar object that is not a valid iTIP message (`calendar_invalid`, `details.reason`) or whose parties do not match the message (`calendar_organizer_mismatch`, `calendar_attendee_mismatch`, `calendar_recipient_mismatch`).

error.message: This endpoint needs an Idempotency-Key header.
error.fix: Send a unique Idempotency-Key per message and reuse it on every retry of that message.

SearchBadRequest.description: The search request is invalid, or `q` could not be parsed (`details.position`, `details.expected`).

error.fix: Close the quoted phrase that starts at position 5.

Unauthorized.description: No key, a malformed or unknown key, or an expired or revoked key.

error.message: No valid API key was provided.
error.fix: Send Authorization: Bearer pmk_live_… with a key created by idvy keys create.

Forbidden.description: The key lacks the permission (`details.required` names it), the resource is outside the key's tenant or identity, the tenant is suspended, or the key's partner is suspended (`partner_suspended`, on every route: a partner key, or a tenant or identity key of one of the partner's tenants).

error.message: This key does not have the messages:send permission.
error.fix: Use a key that holds messages:send.

KeyManageForbidden.description: As `Forbidden`, plus `key_scope_exceeded` when the target key is wider than the caller: a higher level, or a permission the caller does not hold ([J20]).

error.message: This key cannot manage a key that holds permissions it does not hold.
error.fix: Use a key that holds every permission of the target key, or a key of a higher level.

SendForbidden.description: As `Forbidden`, plus `test_mode_recipient` when a test tenant sends to an address that is neither `*@simulator.invalid` nor an identity of its own tenant or of another test tenant with the same partner ([L1], [L3]), and `policy_denied` with `details.reason = "free_sending_off"` when the operator's `free_sending` switch is off and the workspace is on the Free plan or still in its send ramp, or `details.reason = "signup_unverified"` (or `signup_human_unreachable`) when a provisional agent sign-up sends to anyone but its named human, or `signup_paused` for any send of one while the operator's `agent_signup` switch is off. `approval_required` when the tenant's `drafts.require_approval`, or the identity's stricter `send_policy.require_approval`, needs approval for these recipients (`details.reason`, `details.recipients`): nothing was stored; create the message as a draft and send it, and it waits for an approver.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist **or** is outside the key's scope (deliberately indistinguishable). A `404` always carries one of this service's own codes; a `404` without this envelope came from something else and must not be read as "already deleted". `route_not_found` means the path is no route on this host, which says nothing about any resource.

error.message: No such message for this identity.
error.fix: Check the message ID and that the key can reach this identity.

IdempotencyConflict.description: The `Idempotency-Key` was used with a different request (`idempotency_conflict`), or the first request with it is still running (`request_in_progress`, retryable).

SendConflict.description: The send conflicts with the idempotency record or with the identity, thread or domain state. `idempotency_conflict` carries `details.original_message_id` when known; `identity_paused` carries `details.reason`; `thread_busy` carries `details.retry_after`; `loop_detected` carries `details.hop` ([N13]), or `details.reason` (`thread_rate` or `sender_rate`) and `details.retry_after` ([N35]); `sending_paused` carries `details.scope` (`tenant` or `domain`), `details.reason` and, for a domain, `details.domain_id` ([G12]); `calendar_sequence_stale` carries `details.sequence`, `details.latest_sequence` and `details.latest_message_id`; `upload_not_ready` (retryable) carries `details.index` and `details.status` of an attached upload still `pending` or `uploading`. A recipient refused by `send_policy.require_known_recipient` is not an error: its delivery is `suppressed` with `policy: unknown_recipient` ([E2]).

error.message: This Idempotency-Key was used with a different request body.
error.fix: Use a new Idempotency-Key for a different message, or resend the original body.

CalendarReplyConflict.description: The invitation cannot be answered, or the send conflicts with the idempotency record or with the identity, thread or domain state (as `SendConflict`). `calendar_not_invitation` (no readable invitation, or an outbound message; `details.method`, `details.object_status`), `calendar_not_verified` (`details.reason`, `message_quarantined` or `message_screening` for a held invitation), `calendar_not_attendee`, `calendar_cancelled` (`details.cancel_message_id`), `calendar_superseded` (`details.latest_message_id`, `details.latest_sequence`), `calendar_event_past` (`details.ended_at`), `calendar_attendee_address_unavailable` (`details.address`, `details.reason`: `retired`, `pending` or `fallback_pinned`).

MessageExpired.description: The `Idempotency-Key` and body match a send whose message expired under the identity's `retention.message_hours` (`details.message_id`, `details.expired_at`). Nothing was sent.

SendGone.description: As `MessageExpired` (`message_expired`: a retried send whose message expired under the identity's `retention.message_hours`; nothing was sent), or an attached upload expired (`upload_expired`, `details.index`, `details.reason`: `expired`, `too_many_attempts` or `object_missing`; nothing was stored, upload the file again).

CursorExpired.description: The pagination cursor is older than 24 hours (lists): start again from the first page. Or the event cursor or consumer position is behind the retained event log (`details.reason`: `retention`, `size_limit` or `log_reset`; `details.oldest_cursor`; `details.consumer_id` for a consumer).

SendPayloadTooLarge.description: The composed message exceeds the transport limit (5 MiB with Cloudflare; `message_too_large` with `details.reason = "transport_limit"`) and the tenant does not use `large_attachments: link`; or its attachments total more than 26,214,400 decoded bytes (`details.reason = "attachments_total"`, whatever `large_attachments` says); or the request body exceeds 7 MiB (`payload_too_large`); or `calendar.ics` exceeds 262,144 bytes (`calendar_too_large`, `details.limit`).

SendUnprocessable.description: The sending domain's transport is not configured (for example SES for an `external` domain), or a `kind: marketing` message comes from a domain whose transport is `cloudflare` (`details.reason = "marketing_needs_ses"`: Cloudflare Email Service is for transactional mail only). Only a dry run (`dry_run=true`) returns `all_recipients_suppressed` (a real send whose every recipient is suppressed is accepted and ends `suppressed`) and `recipient_blocked` (a recipient is on the send-block list; `details.scope` is `identity` or `tenant`). A calendar message on a `cloudflare` domain before the raw send is available gets `transport_unavailable` with `details.reason = "calendar_needs_raw_mime"`. `attachment_risky`: an attachment, inline or from an upload, carries a quarantining risk (`details.risk`), including after a rename, or the scanner found malware (`details.reason = "infected"`); `details.index` names it.

BillingLimit.description: A plan allowance is spent (`details`: `feature`, `granted`, `used`, `resets_at`, `upgrade_url`). Nothing was stored: upgrade or add a top-up, then retry with the **same** `Idempotency-Key`. Never returned for inbound mail or for the replay of a request that already completed.

error.message: This workspace has used all 12000 sends in its plan for this period.
error.fix: Upgrade the plan or add a sends top-up, then retry with the same Idempotency-Key.

DryRunOk.description: Dry run only (`dry_run=true`): every check passed. Nothing was sent or stored, no quota was taken and the thread was not locked.

LegalHold.description: The operation would delete data under a legal hold.

TooManyRequests.description: A rate limit was hit. Wait `Retry-After` seconds, then retry.

error.message: Too many requests for this API key.
error.fix: Wait for the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then retry with the same Idempotency-Key.

SendTooManyRequests.description: A per-key or per-identity rate limit (`rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`), or a daily cap (`daily_cap_reached`, with `details.cap` and `details.resets_at`): the tenant or identity cap, the shared-domain breaker, or a workspace whose payment is disputed (`resets_at` null). Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

SearchTooManyRequests.description: A search rate limit (`rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`), or the tenant's daily agentic-search budget is spent (`agentic_budget_exhausted`).

NotFrozen.description: The call is allowed only while the deployment is frozen for a restore (`idvy ops freeze`).

InternalError.description: A bug. It is logged with the `request_id`. Retry with backoff.

UpstreamError.description: A Cloudflare or SES API returned an unexpected error during a synchronous call. Retry with backoff.

ServiceUnavailable.description: A dependency is temporarily unavailable (D1, an overloaded Durable Object). Retry with backoff. `details.reason` says when the operator caused it: `frozen` (a restore is in progress; `Retry-After` is 300), `read_only` (an automatic containment rule refused writes) or `storage_full` (the D1 database is full).

SearchUnavailable.description: A dependency is unavailable (`unavailable`), or the request set `require_mode: true` and the requested mode is unavailable (`search_degraded`). Without `require_mode`, search degrades and sets `degraded: true` instead.

GatewayTimeout.description: An internal deadline was exceeded. For sends this happens before the message is queued, so a retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` is safe.

UpgradeRequired.description: `GET /events/stream` without `Upgrade: websocket`. Open it as a WebSocket.

WebhookAccepted.description: Any `2xx` within 15 seconds counts as delivered. The response body is ignored (read up to 4 KB).

WebhookFailed.description: Anything else (including a timeout, TLS or DNS error, redirect or `3xx`) is a failure. Failures retry at about 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 30 min, 1 h, 2 h, 4 h, 8 h, 12 h, 12 h, 12 h and 19 h (±10% jitter, about 72 hours in all), then the delivery is `dead`. The event can be replayed for 30 days from its `occurred_at` (or `retention.events_days`, if shorter), not from when the delivery went dead. After 100 consecutive failures over at least 24 hours the endpoint is disabled (`disabled_reason: failing`).
